# zlantr

> Returns the value of the 1-norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of a trapezoidal or triangular matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlantr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlantr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlantr( order, norm, uplo, diag, M, N, A, LDA, WORK ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANTR as described above. |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the matrix A is upper or lower trapezoidal. `'upper'`: Upper trapezoidal `'lower'`: Lower trapezoidal Note that A is triangular instead of trapezoidal if M = N. |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | Specifies whether or not the matrix A has unit diagonal. `'non-unit'`: Non-unit diagonal `'unit'`: Unit diagonal. |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of rows of the matrix A. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of columns of the matrix A. |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>max(M, 1) × N</sub> | The trapezoidal matrix A (A is triangular if M = N). |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null` | **out** · Caller-provided workspace |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANTR as described above.
- `uplo`: Specifies whether the matrix A is upper or lower trapezoidal.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper trapezoidal
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower trapezoidal Note that A is triangular instead of trapezoidal if $M = N$.
- `diag`: Specifies whether or not the matrix A has unit diagonal.

  -   `= 'N'`: Non-unit diagonal
  -   `= 'U'`: Unit diagonal
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$, and if `UPLO = 'U'`, $M \le N$. When $M = 0$, ZLANTR is set to zero.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$, and if `UPLO = 'L'`, $N \le M$. When $N = 0$, ZLANTR is set to zero.
- `A`: The trapezoidal matrix A (A is triangular if $M = N$). If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading m by n upper trapezoidal part of the array A contains the upper trapezoidal matrix, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading m by n lower trapezoidal part of the array A contains the lower trapezoidal matrix, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. Note that when `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are not referenced and are assumed to be one.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge M$ when `NORM = 'I'`; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: output array

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid diagonal type
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlantr.ndarray(
    norm, uplo, diag,
    M, N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → number
```

Computes the value of a matrix norm for a complex triangular or trapezoidal matrix.

Supports norms: `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, `'frobenius'`.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | Norm type: `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | `'unit'` or `'non-unit'` |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Rows |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Columns |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>max(M, 1) × N</sub> | Complex matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | First dimension stride (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Workspace (length >= M for `'inf-norm'`, real) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANTR as described above.
- `uplo`: Specifies whether the matrix A is upper or lower trapezoidal.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper trapezoidal
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower trapezoidal Note that A is triangular instead of trapezoidal if $M = N$.
- `diag`: Specifies whether or not the matrix A has unit diagonal.

  -   `= 'N'`: Non-unit diagonal
  -   `= 'U'`: Unit diagonal
- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$, and if `UPLO = 'U'`, $M \le N$. When $M = 0$, ZLANTR is set to zero.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$, and if `UPLO = 'L'`, $N \le M$. When $N = 0$, ZLANTR is set to zero.
- `A`: The trapezoidal matrix A (A is triangular if $M = N$). If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading m by n upper trapezoidal part of the array A contains the upper trapezoidal matrix, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading m by n lower trapezoidal part of the array A contains the lower trapezoidal matrix, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced. Note that when `DIAG = 'U'`, the diagonal elements of A are not referenced and are assumed to be one.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge M$ when `NORM = 'I'`; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid diagonal type

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zlantr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlantr';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const WORK = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = zlantr( 'column-major', 'one-norm', 'upper', 'non-unit', N, N, A, N, WORK );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = zlantr.ndarray( 'one-norm', 'upper', 'non-unit', N, N, A, 1, N, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLANTR`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLANTR returns the value of the one norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of a trapezoidal or triangular matrix A.

### Returns

$$
\mathrm{ZLANTR} = \begin{cases} \max (\lvert A(i,j) \rvert) & \text{NORM = 'M' or 'm'} \\ \mathrm{norm1}(A) & \text{NORM = '1', 'O' or 'o'} \\ \mathrm{normI}(A) & \text{NORM = 'I' or 'i'} \\ \mathrm{normF}(A) & \text{NORM = 'F', 'f', 'E' or 'e'} \end{cases}
$$

where norm1 denotes the one norm of a matrix (maximum column sum), normI denotes the infinity norm of a matrix (maximum row sum) and normF denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix (square root of sum of squares). Note that max(abs(`A(i,j)`)) is not a consistent matrix norm.

</section>
